title: Natural comparison of strict derived inverse limit and the product cone
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ be the category of strict inverse sequences with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], and use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a complex $X_\bullet$ of strict towers with transitions $t_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$, put
$$\mathsf C(X_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}\left(1-s:\prod_{n\geq1}X_n\longrightarrow\prod_{n\geq1}X_n\right)[-1],\qquad s((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n.$$
The products here are termwise products of complexes. This construction and its maps from strictly commuting squares descend to a functor $\mathsf C:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to D(\mathcal A)$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\rho_X:\mathsf C(X_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X_\bullet,$$
where $R\lim$ is total derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its normalization is the following: if $q:X_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower resolution with injective terms [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], the canonical inclusion $\lim I_\bullet\to\mathsf C(I_\bullet)$, with zero component in the shifted product, is a quasi-isomorphism, and $\rho_X$ is the class of $\mathsf C(q)$ followed by the inverse of that inclusion. It commutes with each projection to $X_n$.
For a complex $P$ and strictly compatible chain maps $\gamma_n:P\to X_n$, the map $P\to\mathsf C(X_\bullet)$ with product component $(\gamma_n)_n$ and zero shifted-product component corresponds under $\rho_X$ to the canonical derived map $P\to R\lim X_\bullet$ induced by the strict augmentation. This comparison and this assertion are independent of the chosen resolution.

proof.text: Use the signed model $\mathsf C(X)^r=P_X^{r-1}\oplus P_X^r$, $D(y,x)=(-dy-(1-s_X)x,dx)$, where $P_X=\prod_nX_n$. For a strict tower chain map $f:X\to Y$, put $F=\prod_nf_n$. The tower equations give $F(1-s_X)=(1-s_Y)F$ by each product projection. Hence $\mathsf C(f)(y,x)=(Fy,Fx)$ is a chain map, preserving identities and composition. If $h$ is a chain homotopy $f-g=dh+hd$ in the tower category, its termwise product $H$ commutes with shifts of the tower transitions. The map $(y,x)\mapsto(-Hy,Hx)$ of degree $-1$ satisfies $D\widetilde H+\widetilde HD=\mathsf C(f)-\mathsf C(g)$: its off-diagonal terms are $-(1-s_Y)H+H(1-s_X)=0$. Thus the construction also preserves chain homotopies. This uses only the complex, shift and homotopy conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; agent-written strict-cone naturality refinement

proof.text: A quasi-isomorphism $f$ of tower complexes is levelwise a quasi-isomorphism, since the evaluations are exact [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Exactness of countable products and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a)-(c) identify kernels, images and their quotients in the product complex, giving $H^r(P_X)=\prod_nH^r(X_n)$ naturally. Thus $F=\prod_nf_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The strictly commuting square for $1-s$ in step 1 induces a morphism of the shifted cone triangles of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $F$ on both product terms and $\mathsf C(f)$ on the remaining term. The two-product-term isomorphisms imply that $\mathsf C(f)$ is invertible in $D(\mathcal A)$ by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. Therefore $X\mapsto Q\mathsf C(X)$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms and factors through the localization $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the stated action on strict maps.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products, proof; Tag 05RU, definition-derived-category; strict shifted-cone application

proof.text: For resolution existence, form the site with objects $(U,n)$, $n\geq1$, arrows $(U,n)\to(V,m)$ equal to arrows $U\to V$ when $n\leq m$, and coverings at a fixed index inherited from $\mathcal C$. Put $R^{\mathrm{tow}}(U,n)=R(U)$. Its sheaf condition is exactly the sheaf condition at each index; restrictions along $(U,n)\to(U,n+1)$ are the tower transitions. Thus its module sheaves, including their morphisms, are exactly $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$. The site is small in the same universe because a set times $\mathbf N$ is a set, and its ring sheaf is commutative. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to this site to choose a functorial quasi-isomorphism $q_X:X\to I_X$ with $I_X$ K-injective and injective in each degree. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], $L_X=\lim I_X$ computes the specified total derived inverse limit, and on strict maps it is computed by $\lim I(f)$. No boundedness of $X$ is needed.

proof.text: For an injective tower object $J$, let $T_n(M)$ equal $M$ through index $n$, with identity transitions, and zero above $n$. A tower map $T_n(M)\to J$ is determined by its component $M\to J_n$. The inclusion $T_n(M)\hookrightarrow T_{n+1}(M)$ is monic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. With $M=J_n$, extend the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{J_n}$ across this inclusion by injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Its component at $n+1$ is a section $\sigma_n$ of $J_{n+1}\to J_n$. Apply this separately to each injective tower $I^r$. In degree $r$, the recursion $y_1=0$, $y_{n+1}=\sigma_n(y_n-x_n)$ defines, coordinate by coordinate using finite sums, a morphism $x\mapsto y$ on $P_I^r=\prod_n I_n^r$ with $(1-s_I)y=x$. Thus $u=1-s_I$ is degreewise split epic and its kernel is the compatible-family complex $L=\lim_n I_n$. The sections need not commute with the differential; only the degreewise epimorphism assertion is used.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, injective-tower transition and short exact sequence paragraphs; explicit extension argument for modules

proof.text: For the degreewise epimorphism $u=1-s_I:P_I\to P_I$ of step 4, the compatible-family inclusion $\eta:L\to\mathsf C(I)$ is $z\mapsto(0,z)$. Its quotient complex is identified degreewise with $E^r=P_I^{r-1}\oplus P_I^r$ by $[(y,x)]\mapsto(y,ux)$, since $\ker u=L$ and $u$ is epic. As $u$ commutes with differentials, $D_E(y,z)=(-dy-z,dz)$. The degree $-1$ map $h(y,z)=(0,-y)$ satisfies $D_Eh+hD_E=1$: the two summands are $(y,-dy)$ and $(0,dy+z)$. Hence $E$ is contractible and zero in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to $0\to L\xrightarrow{\eta}\mathsf C(I)\to E\to0$. The maps $(1,Q\eta,0)$ from the distinguished identity triangle $QL\xrightarrow{1}QL\to0\to QL[1]$ to this triangle commute in all three squares; the last two have zero source or target. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], $Q\eta$ is invertible. Put $\rho_X=(Q\eta)^{-1}Q\mathsf C(q_X)$, using step 3 to identify $QL$ with $R\lim X$. The equalities $p_{I,n}\eta=\mathrm{pr}_n$ and $p_{I,n}\mathsf C(q_X)=q_{X,n}p_{X,n}$ give $e_n\rho_X=p_{X,n}$, where $e_n=(Qq_{X,n})^{-1}Q\mathrm{pr}_n$.

proof.text: For a strict chain map $f:X\to Y$, functoriality of the chosen resolution gives $I(f)q_X=q_Yf$. The map on inverse limits is the restriction of $\prod_nI(f)_n$ to compatible families. Consequently the identity $\mathsf C(I(f))\eta_X=\eta_Y\lim I(f)$ holds as chain maps, since both send $z$ to $(0,(I(f)_nz_n)_n)$. Combining it with $\mathsf C(I(f))\mathsf C(q_X)=\mathsf C(q_Y)\mathsf C(f)$ and cancelling the invertible $\eta$ gives $(R\lim f)\rho_X=\rho_Y\mathsf C(f)$. Here [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] identifies the limit map with the actual derived functor map. By the localization description in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived morphisms are generated by chain maps and formal inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. The equation for a quasi-isomorphism implies the equation for its inverse by cancellation, and equations compose. Thus $\rho$ is natural on the whole derived category.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; agent-written strict-cone naturality refinement

proof.text: Let $q:X\to I$ and $q':X\to J$ be any two K-injective tower resolutions with injective terms. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied in the abelian tower category, gives a chain map $a:I\to J$ with $aq$ homotopic to $q'$, uniquely up to homotopy. Its derived class is $Q(q')Q(q)^{-1}$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism and the same lemma makes it a homotopy equivalence. Applying termwise limit to its inverse and homotopies gives the canonical identification of the limit models from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The coordinate identity $\mathsf C(a)\eta_I=\eta_J\lim a$ and Step 1's homotopy preservation imply, after localization and cancellation, $Q(\lim a)Q(\eta_I)^{-1}Q\mathsf C(q)=Q(\eta_J)^{-1}Q\mathsf C(q')$. Step 5 proves both $\eta_I$ and $\eta_J$ are quasi-isomorphisms by the quotient contraction, so this is the canonical resolution-independent comparison and normalization formula.

source.place: Tag 070I K-injective comparison; Tag 0941 resolution computation; explicit strict-cone coordinate calculation

proof.text: For the strict augmentation $\gamma_n:P\to X_n$, compatibility says $(1-s_X)\gamma=0$ for $\gamma=(\gamma_n)_n:P\to P_X$. Thus $b:P\to\mathsf C(X)$, $b(p)=(0,\gamma(p))$ in the signed coordinate order of step 1, is a chain map. The family $q_n\gamma_n$ is still strictly compatible, hence determines the chain map $\lambda:P\to\lim I_n$. Directly on the two coordinates, $\mathsf C(q)b=\eta_I\lambda$. It follows that $\rho_XQ(b)=Q(\lambda)$ in the derived-limit model $Q\lim I_n$. The latter is the canonical derived map induced by the strict augmentation: take its compatible maps into the chosen tower resolution and apply the ordinary limit universal property, as in the resolution computation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. This also fixes its zero shifted-product component. For another resolution the $a$ of step 7 satisfies $aq\gamma\sim q'\gamma$; their compatible homotopies restrict to inverse limits. Thus the same canonical comparison identifies both $Q\lambda$, proving independence of this assertion as well.
